c.v: Solar shingle installation

runs.v: replaces a roof covering with building-integrated photovoltaic shingles that generate electricity while serving as the roof itself. The photovoltaic material is the roof surface, distinct from rack-mounted panels added on top of a finished roof.

Solar shingles replace traditional roofing materials with photovoltaic shingles, so every solar shingle installation Newark NJ homeowners plan is a roof replacement first and a solar power project second. The work takes specialized expertise in both roofing and electrical work, and the wiring belongs to a New Jersey licensed electrical contractor.

sections.heading: Solar Shingles vs. Solar Panels: Should You Install Solar Panels or a Nailable Solar Shingle?

c.v: Solar shingles are less efficient and cost more per watt than solar panels: solar shingle modules cluster around 14% to 18% efficiency, while premium panels typically exceed 20%, per NREL.

runs.v: Solar shingles generate about 16.7 watts per square foot and roughly 57 to 72 watts per shingle or tile, less electricity per square foot than panels, so they need about 44% more roof area for the same system. Solar panels are mounted on top of existing roofs and can last 25 to 30 years; solar shingles are often estimated to last about 20 years, roughly matching an asphalt shingle roof, and durability and warranties vary by product. A nailable solar shingle fastens into an asphalt-shingle field like a standard shingle, with each energy shingle wired into the array, while full-replacement glass solar tiles cover the whole roof with matching inactive tiles. Crystalline silicon solar shingles are the most efficient type; thin-film solar shingles are lightweight and flexible but produce less power.

For a Newark house, the deciding questions are roof age, roof shape, sun, and appearance. A solar shingle makes the most sense on a pitched roof that needs replacing anyway, with a slope in direct sunlight, where looks matter. Flat roofs on many Newark row houses and multi-family buildings take rack-mounted or ballasted panels instead, and a sound roof with years of life left is usually better served by panels. Solar shingles are one of several energy efficient solutions a reroof can include, and they can increase home value by reducing energy bills, with energy savings that depend on system size, sun exposure, and electricity use.

Code-Compliant Wiring and Rapid Shutdown

c.v: The electrical side of a solar roof is coordinated with a New Jersey licensed electrical contractor.

runs.v: Solar installations require compliance with the National Electrical Code, and New Jersey enforces its rapid shutdown requirements: NEC 690.12 drops conductors to 30 volts or less outside the array boundary and 80 volts or less inside it within 30 seconds, using module-level electronics or a listed UL 3741 system. The 33% rule for solar panels comes from IRC R324.6: an array covering 33 percent or less of the roof needs an 18-inch ridge setback, a larger one 36 inches; the code official decides how it applies to a building-integrated roof.

sections.heading: New Jersey Solar Installation Incentives in 2026: Is There a Federal Tax Credit for Solar Shingles?

c.v: No federal residential solar tax credit applies to a solar shingle system completed after December 31, 2025.

runs.v: The IRS states the Residential Clean Energy Credit equaled 30% of the cost of qualified property installed from 2022 through December 31, 2025, and is not allowed for expenditures made after that date, which the IRS treats as made when installation is completed. For business-owned solar, the federal Section 48E credit ends for solar facilities placed in service after 2027 when construction began after July 4, 2026, per the IRS Form 3468 instructions.

New Jersey programs remain. The NJ Board of Public Utilities' Successor Solar Incentive (SuSI) program provides a fixed per-megawatt-hour SREC-II incentive over a 15-year term, and a May 2026 Board order kept its ADI registration open until June 1, 2027 or until each capacity block fills. Net metering allows homeowners to receive credits for excess electricity sent to the grid, solar energy equipment is exempt from New Jersey sales tax with Form ST-4, and a certified renewable energy system can qualify for a limited property-tax exemption on Form CRES. These programs apply statewide, from Essex County to Bergen County; confirm current terms at njcleanenergy.com and with a tax professional.

faqs.q: Should you repair or replace an old roof before solar shingles?

runs.v: Replace it as one project. A solar shingle is building-integrated photovoltaics that serve as the roof covering, so the old roof comes off and the solar shingles go on with the new roof.

faqs.q: How much roof area does a solar shingle roofing system need?

runs.v: A 6-kilowatt solar-shingle system needs about 360 square feet of shingles against about 250 square feet of panels, roughly 44% more roof area.

faqs.q: How much does a solar shingle installation cost in Essex County, NJ?

runs.v: Solar shingles cost about $3.50 to $8.00 per watt installed against about $2.50 to $4.00 per watt for rack-mounted panels, and the reroof is part of the project.

faqs.q: What are the disadvantages of solar shingles?

runs.v: Higher cost per watt, lower efficiency, about 44% more roof area for the same output, fewer products and installers, repairs that need a crew trained on the system, and a longer install: weeks, compared with hours to a day for a rack-mounted array on a sound roof.
